name: Hanan

title: Ethiopian plate basics for everyday health
author: Abinet Tekle Hagos
excerpt: A simple way to build balanced plates using injera, legumes, vegetables, and familiar Ethiopian flavors.

content.heading: Start with what you already eat
content.body: Healthy eating does not require abandoning Ethiopian cuisine. Injera, shiro, lentils, greens, and vegetable wot can anchor a balanced day when portions and variety are intentional.

content.heading: Build color and protein into the plate
content.body: Aim for vegetables or legumes alongside staples, and notice how energy and fullness change when meals include fiber-rich sides. Personal targets differ — counseling can refine this for you.

content.heading: When to get personal guidance
content.body: If you manage a medical condition, are pregnant, or need a structured plan, book a consultation rather than relying on general articles alone.

title: Sustainable habits for weight management
author: Abinet Tekle Hagos
excerpt: Why slow, personalized changes beat extreme diets — and how to think about progress without miracle promises.

content.heading: Habits over hacks
content.body: Sustainable weight management focuses on routines you can keep: meal rhythm, sleep, movement you enjoy, and food patterns that fit your culture and schedule.

content.heading: No guaranteed outcomes
content.body: NEED does not promise specific kilogram results. Progress depends on many factors and should be reviewed individually with appropriate clinical care when needed.

content.heading: Next step
content.body: If you want a personalized plan, use Book a Consultation. For workplace programs, use the partnerships pathway instead.

title: Diabetes-friendly Ethiopian meal ideas
author: NEED Nutritional
excerpt: Practical plate ideas that respect Ethiopian food culture while supporting diabetes nutrition education.

content.heading: Education, not treatment
content.body: Nutrition counseling supports diabetes care but never replaces medication or instructions from your clinician. Do not change prescriptions based on an article.

content.heading: Familiar foods, thoughtful patterns
content.body: Balanced plates, consistent meal timing, and awareness of carbohydrate patterns can be discussed using foods you already know — injera, legumes, vegetables, and dairy where appropriate.

content.heading: Get tailored support
content.body: Book a diabetes nutrition consultation for guidance matched to your clinician’s plan and your daily routine.

title: Sodium-aware cooking at home
author: NEED Nutritional
excerpt: Simple kitchen swaps and seasoning ideas to support blood-pressure-conscious cooking without bland meals.

content.heading: Flavor without excess salt
content.body: Herbs, spices, garlic, lemon, and careful use of berbere-style blends can keep meals enjoyable while you watch sodium — always within your clinician’s guidance.

content.heading: Cooking patterns that help
content.body: Cooking more at home, tasting before adding salt, and balancing vegetables with staples are practical starting points for many households.

content.heading: Personalize with NEED
content.body: Hypertension nutrition counseling can turn these ideas into a plan that fits your household and medical care.

title: Fiber, fats, and heart-conscious eating
author: Abinet Tekle Hagos
excerpt: A calm overview of dietary patterns that support lipid health — without extreme elimination diets.

content.heading: Patterns matter more than perfection
content.body: Fiber-rich legumes, vegetables, and balanced fat choices can support heart-conscious eating. Extreme elimination is rarely the first or best step.

content.heading: Work with your clinician
content.body: Lab results and medication decisions belong with your medical team. Nutrition education complements — it does not replace — clinical care.

content.heading: Go deeper
content.body: Explore cholesterol nutrition services or book a consultation for a personalized approach.

title: Nutrition in pregnancy — basics
author: NEED Nutritional
excerpt: General education on nourishing pregnancy with familiar foods — always alongside antenatal clinical care.

content.heading: Clinical care comes first
content.body: Pregnancy nutrition articles are educational only. Follow your antenatal clinician’s advice for supplements, screening, and medical decisions.

content.heading: Steady, diverse meals
content.body: Regular meals with vegetables, legumes, staples, and adequate fluids support many pregnancies. Individual needs vary widely.

content.heading: Ask for tailored counseling
content.body: NEED can provide personalized maternal nutrition counseling when appropriate — never as a substitute for obstetric care.

title: Feeding toddlers with local foods
author: NEED Nutritional
excerpt: Ideas for introducing diverse Ethiopian family foods to young children — gently and safely.

content.heading: Family foods, age-appropriate textures
content.body: Many Ethiopian household foods can be adapted for toddlers with safe textures and gradual introduction. Watch for choking risks and follow pediatric guidance.

content.heading: Growth is individual
content.body: Appetite and growth patterns differ. Use your child’s clinician for growth concerns; use NEED for general nutrition education and meal planning support where relevant.

content.heading: Language note
content.body: Amharic clinical guidance should be human-reviewed before publication. This English draft is a placeholder structure for CMS content.

title: Reading nutrition labels — simply
author: NEED Nutritional
excerpt: A plain-language walkthrough of packaged-food labels so you can compare products with less confusion.

content.heading: What to glance at first
content.body: Serving size, energy, and key nutrients help you compare similar products. Labels are tools — not moral judgments about food.

content.heading: Context beats fear
content.body: One packaged item rarely makes or breaks a diet. Patterns across days and weeks matter more than a single label.

content.heading: Need a plan?
content.body: General nutrition counseling can help you apply label literacy to your real shopping and cooking routine.

title: Sewegna recap: green vegetables on the Ethiopian plate
author: Sewegna / NEED
excerpt: A written recap of Sewegna themes on traditional greens — collards, cabbage, Swiss chard — and everyday cooking.

content.heading: From screen to kitchen
content.body: Sewegna conversations often return to Ethiopia’s green vegetables — affordable, familiar, and central to many traditional meals.

content.heading: Campaign echoes
content.body: Public campaigns such as Green Gursha highlighted greens alongside culinary heritage. Recaps here summarize education themes, not medical outcomes.

content.heading: Watch more
content.body: Visit the Sewegna archive for video episodes, and book a consultation if you want personalized meal guidance.
